issues.legal_issue: A restricted statutory appeal may involve a substantial question of law when it challenges a finding on whether a landlord’s residential requirement is bona fide, because that finding is a mixed question of law and fact.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction on the ground that the premises were bona fide required as a residence for himself and his family.
The Rent Controller and the appellate Tribunal rejected the landlord’s claim, reasoning that he should have anticipated his need for additional accommodation when he let part of the premises.
On remand, the Tribunal found that the landlord’s existing accommodation was not reasonably suitable for his family.
The High Court considered the concurrent rejection of the landlord’s claim erroneous and allowed the eviction application.
issues.conclusion: The High Court did not exceed its jurisdiction by reviewing the subordinate authorities’ finding on bona fide requirement; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 39(2) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, an appeal lies only if it involves a substantial question of law. As held in Smt. Kamla Soni v. Rup Lal Mehra, whether a landlord’s requirement is bona fide under section 14(1)(e) is a mixed question of law and fact, so the subordinate authorities’ finding is not conclusive and the High Court may review it in a proper case. Bhagwan Dass v. S. Rajdev Singh concerned a concurrent factual finding of subletting reached after considering the relevant evidence and did not bar review of a mixed question of law and fact.

predicates.restricted_rent_control_appeal: A party brought a restricted appeal from a rent-control decision to a High Court.
predicates.bona_fide_residential_requirement_at_iss: The appeal concerned whether a landlord genuinely required premises as a residence for the landlord or a dependent family member.
predicates.lower_courts_used_anticipated_need_as_ba: The lower courts rejected the claimed need because they considered that the landlord should have anticipated it when letting the premises.
predicates.existing_accommodation_found_unsuitable: A finding was made that the landlord’s existing residential accommodation was not reasonably suitable for the household.

issues.definition: When a restricted rent-control appeal concerns the bona fide nature of a landlord’s residential need and either stated circumstance applies, the High Court may review the finding.
